text: First, sit Ben in a barrel, tie on a big rock, and push.
Down he goes... Congratulations, you've built a submarine!
Mm-mmm!
It can go down. It just can't come back up.
Water pushes up with the weight of the water you push aside.
The rock weighs more than that, so it sinks.
A beach ball weighs much less, so it pops right back up.
Whoa-oh!
So heavy things sink, light things float, and the same weight hovers.
So you build a sub that can change its weight,
with two empty tanks on the sides.
Fishing time!
Full of air, it floats.
Open the vents, the tanks fill with water, and down it goes.
Too much water, and it sinks to the bottom.
Pump half the water out, and it weighs exactly as much as the water it pushes aside,
so it just hangs there in the water, perfectly still.
A propeller at the back pushes it along, past the weeds.
And a periscope pokes up to look around.
And who's that up there? It's the neighbour, fishing.
Then his fishing hook snags the sub.
Big one!
Ben drives off, towing him across the lake.
Biggest catch of my life!
Deeper down, the water presses harder, one more atmosphere every ten metres.
It's getting tight in here... AAAH!
So Ben blows the tanks with compressed air,
now it's lighter than the water, and up it shoots,
right up under the neighbour's little boat. Oops.
Empty tanks: it floats again.
Worst fishing trip ever.
And there you have it. Congratulations, you've built a submarine!
You know they sell snorkels, dear?
Now you tell me.
